input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I’ve been trying to send a picture message—what I think you call an MMS?—but it just won’t go through. This has been happening for a few hours now. Can you help me fix it?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.

I’m not sure about the calls or data right now, but I do see a little airplane icon at the top of my screen. Does that mean something important? I haven’t noticed any specific error messages, it just won’t send the picture. I’m not sure if I’m on Wi-Fi or mobile data either—how can I check that?

Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode like you said, but I still can’t send a picture message. I don’t see the airplane icon anymore, but now there’s something that looks like “no signal” at the top. What should I do next?
I checked, and it says there’s no SIM card detected in my phone. I’m not sure what to do about that—does that mean something is wrong with my phone, or do I need to do something else?

Alright, I followed your instructions and took out the SIM card, then put it back in. Now my phone shows a signal again, and it says “2G” at the top. But I still can’t send a picture message. Is there something else I should try?

I changed the network mode like you said, and now it shows “5G” at the top with a strong signal. But I still can’t send a picture message—it just won’t go through. Is there anything else I should try? I’m starting to get a bit frustrated.

I reset the APN settings and restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send a picture message. It’s still not working, and I’m getting a bit worried—am I doing something wrong? I really just want to send this photo to my family.

It looks like Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned on. Should I go ahead and turn that off now? Also, I see I have a messaging app and a browser—do you want me to check the permissions for the messaging app too, or just focus on the Wi-Fi Calling for now? I just want to make sure I’m doing this right.

I turned off Wi-Fi Calling like you said, but I still can’t send a picture message. Should I check the permissions for my messaging app now? If so, could you walk me through how to do that? I get a bit nervous with these settings.

I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it looks like it only has permission for “phone.” I don’t see anything about storage or SMS being allowed. How do I turn those on? I’m worried I might mess something up.

I turned on both the storage and SMS permissions for my messaging app, but I still can’t send a picture message. Is there anything else I can try? I’m starting to feel a bit overwhelmed by all these steps.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I’ve been trying to send a picture message—what I think you call an MMS?—but it just won’t go through. This has been happening for a few hours now. Can you help me fix it?

Thank you for reaching out about your MMS issue. I can help you troubleshoot this problem.

To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth (in YYYY-MM-DD format), or
- Your customer ID (if you have it)?

Once I have this information, I can assist you further.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.

Thank you for providing your information. I’ve identified your account. To help you send picture messages (MMS), I’ll need to check a few things about your phone and service.

Could you please let me know:
- Are you able to make regular calls and use mobile data (like browsing the web)?
- Are you currently connected to Wi-Fi or using mobile data?
- Have you noticed any error messages when trying to send the MMS?

This information will help me guide you through the right troubleshooting steps.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%

I’m not sure about the calls or data right now, but I do see a little airplane icon at the top of my screen. Does that mean something important? I haven’t noticed any specific error messages, it just won’t send the picture. I’m not sure if I’m on Wi-Fi or mobile data either—how can I check that?

The airplane icon means your phone is in Airplane Mode, which disables all wireless connections—including calls, mobile data, and MMS. This is likely why your picture message isn’t sending.

Here’s what you should do:
1. Turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. You can usually do this by swiping down from the top of your screen and tapping the airplane icon, or by going to your phone’s settings and toggling Airplane Mode off.
2. Once Airplane Mode is off, wait a few seconds for your phone to reconnect to the network.
3. Try sending your picture message again.

After you’ve done this, let me know if the MMS goes through or if you see any new icons or messages at the top of your screen. If it still doesn’t work, I’ll guide you through checking your Wi-Fi and mobile data status.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode like you said, but I still can’t send a picture message. I don’t see the airplane icon anymore, but now there’s something that looks like “no signal” at the top. What should I do next?

Thank you for the update. Since you now see a “no signal” icon, it means your phone isn’t currently connected to the cellular network, which is required for sending MMS.

Let’s check your SIM card status next, as a SIM issue can cause loss of signal. Please follow these steps on your phone:
1. Go to your phone’s settings.
2. Find the section for “SIM card” or “Mobile network.”
3. Look for any messages about the SIM card being missing, locked, or inactive.

If you see an option to “reseat” or “reinsert” your SIM card, please try that. Remove the SIM card (if possible), wait a few seconds, and reinsert it securely.

After you’ve checked or reseated your SIM card, let me know if your signal returns or if you see any new messages or icons. If you’re unsure how to check your SIM status, let me know your phone model and I can provide more specific instructions.
No SIM card detected in the phone.
I checked, and it says there’s no SIM card detected in my phone. I’m not sure what to do about that—does that mean something is wrong with my phone, or do I need to do something else?

If your phone says there’s no SIM card detected, it usually means the SIM card is either not properly inserted, has shifted out of place, or there’s a temporary connection issue. This is a common cause for losing signal and being unable to send MMS.

Here’s what you should do:
1. Power off your phone completely.
2. Locate the SIM card tray (usually on the side or back of your phone).
3. Remove the SIM card tray and take out the SIM card.
4. Carefully reinsert the SIM card, making sure it’s seated properly and securely in the tray.
5. Put the tray back in and power your phone back on.

After your phone restarts, check if the signal returns and if the phone now detects the SIM card. Try sending your picture message again.

Let me know if this resolves the issue or if your phone still says “no SIM card detected.”

SIM card re-seated successfully.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

Alright, I followed your instructions and took out the SIM card, then put it back in. Now my phone shows a signal again, and it says “2G” at the top. But I still can’t send a picture message. Is there something else I should try?

Great job reseating the SIM card! Now that you have a signal, but your phone shows “2G,” this could be the reason MMS still isn’t working—MMS usually requires at least a 3G or higher connection.

Please change your network mode to prefer 4G or 5G (if your phone supports it). Here’s how you can do this:
1. Go to your phone’s Settings.
2. Find “Mobile Network” or “Cellular Network.”
3. Look for “Preferred network type” or “Network mode.”
4. Select an option like “4G/5G preferred” or “4G/3G/2G (auto connect).”

After changing the network mode, wait a few moments for your phone to connect to a higher-speed network. Once you see “3G,” “4G,” or “5G” at the top of your screen, try sending your picture message again.

Let me know if you’re able to change the network mode and if this helps with sending MMS. If you need step-by-step instructions for your specific phone model, let me know!

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

I changed the network mode like you said, and now it shows “5G” at the top with a strong signal. But I still can’t send a picture message—it just won’t go through. Is there anything else I should try? I’m starting to get a bit frustrated.

Thank you for your patience and for following the steps so far. Since you now have a strong 5G signal but still can’t send MMS, the next most common cause is an issue with your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings, which are required for MMS to work.

Please follow these steps:
1. Go to your phone’s Settings.
2. Find “Mobile Network” or “Cellular Network.”
3. Look for “Access Point Names” or “APN.”
4. If you see an option to “Reset to default” or “Reset settings,” please select it.

After resetting your APN settings, you must restart your phone for the changes to take effect. Please power off your phone, wait a few seconds, and then turn it back on.

Once your phone restarts, try sending your picture message again.

Let me know if this resolves the issue or if you still have trouble sending MMS. If it still doesn’t work, I’ll continue to help you troubleshoot.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

I reset the APN settings and restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send a picture message. It’s still not working, and I’m getting a bit worried—am I doing something wrong? I really just want to send this photo to my family.

You’re doing everything right, and I appreciate your patience. Since you have a strong signal, correct network mode, and have reset your APN settings, let’s check a few more things that can affect MMS:

1. Is Wi-Fi Calling enabled on your phone? Sometimes, having Wi-Fi Calling turned on can interfere with MMS. Please check your phone’s settings for “Wi-Fi Calling” and, if it’s on, try turning it off.
2. Does your messaging app have permission to access storage and SMS? Go to your phone’s app settings, find your messaging app, and make sure it has permission to access storage (for photos) and SMS.

Please check these two things and let me know:
- If Wi-Fi Calling was on and you turned it off, try sending the picture message again.
- If you had to change app permissions, try sending the message again after granting them.

If you’re unsure how to check these settings, let me know your phone model and I can provide step-by-step instructions. We’ll get this working for you!
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON.
The following apps are installed on the phone: messaging, browser

It looks like Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned on. Should I go ahead and turn that off now? Also, I see I have a messaging app and a browser—do you want me to check the permissions for the messaging app too, or just focus on the Wi-Fi Calling for now? I just want to make sure I’m doing this right.

Yes, please go ahead and turn off Wi-Fi Calling first, as this is a common cause of MMS issues. After turning it off, try sending your picture message again.

If it still doesn’t work after turning off Wi-Fi Calling, then check the permissions for your messaging app. Make sure it has access to both storage and SMS.

Let me know what happens after you turn off Wi-Fi Calling and try to send the MMS. If needed, I’ll guide you through checking app permissions next.

Wi-Fi Calling is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

I turned off Wi-Fi Calling like you said, but I still can’t send a picture message. Should I check the permissions for my messaging app now? If so, could you walk me through how to do that? I get a bit nervous with these settings.

Absolutely, I can guide you step-by-step to check your messaging app’s permissions. Here’s how you can do it (these steps work for most Android phones—if you have an iPhone or a different device, let me know):

1. Open your phone’s Settings app.
2. Scroll down and tap on “Apps” or “Applications.”
3. Find and tap on your messaging app (it might be called “Messages,” “Messaging,” or something similar).
4. Tap on “Permissions.”
5. Make sure both “Storage” and “SMS” permissions are enabled (the switches should be ON or toggled to allow).

If either permission is off, tap it and select “Allow.”

After you’ve checked and enabled these permissions, try sending your picture message again.

Let me know if you need more detailed instructions for your specific phone model, or if you run into any issues during these steps. We’re almost there!
App 'messaging' has permission for: phone.

I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it looks like it only has permission for “phone.” I don’t see anything about storage or SMS being allowed. How do I turn those on? I’m worried I might mess something up.

No worries—granting these permissions is safe and necessary for your messaging app to send and receive picture messages. Here’s how you can enable “Storage” and “SMS” permissions:

1. In your phone’s Settings, go to “Apps” or “Applications.”
2. Find and tap on your messaging app.
3. Tap on “Permissions.”
4. You should see a list of permissions, some under “Allowed” and some under “Denied.”
5. Tap on “Storage” and select “Allow.”
6. Tap on “SMS” and select “Allow.”

If you don’t see “Storage” or “SMS” listed, look for an option like “See all permissions” or “Additional permissions.”

Once you’ve enabled both permissions, try sending your picture message again.

Let me know if you have any trouble finding these options, or if you need instructions for a different phone type. You’re doing great!

Success. Permission 'storage' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Success. Permission 'sms' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

I turned on both the storage and SMS permissions for my messaging app, but I still can’t send a picture message. Is there anything else I can try? I’m starting to feel a bit overwhelmed by all these steps.

Thank you for your patience and for following all the steps so far. Since you have tried all the standard troubleshooting steps—checking signal, network mode, APN settings, Wi-Fi Calling, and app permissions—and the issue still persists, this may require more advanced technical support.

I will transfer you to a human agent who can assist you further and ensure your MMS issue is resolved.
